Use the `snapshot` from [source observations](source-observations.qmd). This
branch asks for Electrostatic terminal response rather than resonant modes.
The public OrPen [Xmon notebook group](../examples.qmd#public-inputs) owns the
component example; this lesson explains the reusable SCGSim stages.

A Terminal identifies a conductor Net whose excitation enters the native
matrix. Physical Ground identifies other conductor Nets. Grounding the outer
solution boundary is a separate physical choice, not another spelling of a
conductor ground. Here the Xmon pad is the terminal and its already assigned
`Ground` Net is the physical ground:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.palace import ElectrostaticSim

sim = ElectrostaticSim()
sim.set_plan(snapshot)
sim.set_output_dir(Path(".artifacts/public-xmon-electrostatic"))
sim.add_terminal("xmon", net_id="xmon_pad")
sim.add_ground(net_id="Ground")
sim.set_electrostatic(
    save_fields=0,
    unassigned_conductor_policy="error",
    exterior_boundary_policy="none",
)
sim.set_mesh(refined_mesh_size=5.0, max_mesh_size=300.0)
```

The terminal and ground selectors are exact final Net IDs. They are not
geometric center guesses. The explicit `error` policy makes uncovered conductor
components an input error; the alternative supported `ground` policy grounds
unassigned components. Choose the policy for your experiment. The exterior is
left ungrounded here; `exterior_boundary_policy="ground"` is a separate model
and requires the explicit error policy. [The contract](../specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd)
owns these choices and their index-map meaning.

## Select the geometry approximation and build inputs

The bound snapshot already supplies the outer envelope. Route B is the default
finite-metal preparation. To explicitly select it without requesting surface
films:

```python
sim.set_surface_epr(representation="B", specs={})
mesh_path = sim.mesh()
config_path = sim.write_config()
print(mesh_path, config_path)
```

For a Route-A study, configure `representation="A"` with the appropriate
explicit `route_a_thin_film` before meshing. `substrate_face` preserves physical
face coordinates; `metal_gap_equivalent` is the separate supported two-face
normalization. Consult the [geometry contract](../geometry-sgb.qmd) before
changing that approximation. Surface films and their native inset margins are
optional postprocessing specifications, with attributed thickness/permittivity/
loss assumptions rather than inferred material measurements.

The mesh is a real preparation operation and can fail natively. Writing config
binds terminal and Ground attributes to that mesh. Inspect the exact index map
alongside the config: schema v2 distinguishes physical Ground from exterior
Ground, so you can tell which conductor and boundary policy was lowered.
The [source summary](source-observations.qmd) remains a separate input view;
`ElectrostaticSim` has no `input_summary()` method.

Next [inspect the prepared mesh](solver-observations.qmd) if useful, then
[prepare and execute the handoff](execute.qmd). On return,
[resolve it](returned-results.qmd) before reading the capacitance matrix. Native
terminal/excitation ordering and units remain authoritative; a prepared config
contains no measured capacitance.
